audit_findings.title: The $231.4m stakes bridge likely double-counts earnings already in owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: The operating valuation capitalizes unconsolidated-JV and affiliate earnings already included in OE, while the bridge adds the associated investment balances again.
audit_findings.evidence: If we have determined that we are not the primary beneficiary of a joint venture but do exercise significant influence, we account for our share of the operations of unconsolidated construction joint ventures on a pro rata basis in revenue and cost of revenue in the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated double-counting error: the $134.670m construction-JV balance plus $96.764m of affiliate investments approximately equals the $231.4m bridge. Removing the entire amount would reduce base value from $60.10 to about $55.98 per share and bull value from $67.24 to about $63.12. Because it only lowers values already far below the $119.30 market price, it does not change the no-buy valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Decompose stakes_net, remove the performance-guarantee gross-up, and rerun using either purged OE plus realizable investment value or unpurged OE with no stakes bridge.

audit_findings.title: The 3.25% note dilution assumes shares for principal that must be paid in cash
audit_findings.magnitude: 4.798875m excess full-conversion shares; removing all would raise base value to about $65.72 and bull value to about $73.53 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The full conversion rate is included in diluted shares even though the $373.75m principal must be cash-settled; only conversion-premium shares, net of capped-call protection, can dilute equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, we will settle the principal amount of the 3.25 % Convertible Notes in cash, and any conversion premium in excess of the principal amount in cash, shares of common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of common stock, at our election.
audit_findings.explanation: The settlement-language conflict is demonstrated. The 4.798875m shares are 9.3% of the 51.337382m denominator remaining after their removal. Even the maximum upward correction of removing all those shares leaves the bull value about $45.77 below the $119.30 market price, so it cannot change the no-buy conclusion. Actual dilution may be above zero because premium settlement and capped-call outcomes must still be modeled.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the 3.25% notes using treasury-stock-equivalent premium dilution at the valuation price, apply the $119.82 capped-call cap, and reconcile interest treatment separately from the 3.75% notes.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor is on a partial-year acquisition perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: A partial-period OE anchor is forecast against a later balance-sheet bridge containing the acquired assets, cash and financing, so sustainable OE, interest, taxes and maintenance capital are not measured on one perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 5, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Warren Paving for $ 540.0 million in cash, subject to customary closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its OE effect is unresolved. Warren Paving, Papich and Cinderlite contributed only $218.6m of FY2025 revenue and $26.6m of gross profit after their acquisition dates, while their aggregate stated cash purchase prices were $768.5m. The June 2026 perimeter also includes the $163.6m Kenny Seng acquisition. Filed pro formas do not supply a complete post-acquisition OE figure, so the record cannot establish whether the correction is large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Construct a post-acquisition LTM or combined full-year pro forma including every acquired business, acquisition financing, taxes, eligible D&A and maintenance capital, then rerun all scenarios and the bridge on the same date.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow adjustments may not belong entirely to parent shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 excluded $27.348m of NCI income while filed D&A of $162.433m and capex of $138.270m were consolidated
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with consolidated D&A, capex and other adjustments, potentially assigning the noncontrolling partners' portion of those cash-flow items to Granite's OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount attributable to non-controlling interests represents the non-controlling owners’ share of the net (income) loss of our consolidated construction joint ventures.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-perimeter mismatch is demonstrated if the valuation used the consolidated cash-flow adjustments without allocation. Its direction and size cannot be established because the filing does not disclose the CCJV portions of eligible D&A and maintenance capex. The $27.348m NCI income allocation shows that the ownership difference is potentially meaningful relative to the $158.6m anchor, but it does not quantify the net OE correction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level CCJV D&A, capex and other OE adjustments; allocate them by Granite's economic interest, or calculate consolidated OE and explicitly deduct the NCI claim before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may include joint-venture cash unavailable to Granite shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.637m partner share; an additional $95.9m Granite share was unavailable until distribution
audit_findings.mechanism: The $913.973m cash-and-STI bridge includes $154.537m of CCJV cash, although only $95.9m is Granite's economic share and even that amount requires joint approval for distribution.
audit_findings.evidence: The decision to distribute joint venture assets must generally be made jointly by a majority of the members and, accordingly, these assets, including those associated with estimated cost recovery of customer affirmative claims and back charge claims, are generally not available for the working capital needs of Granite until distributed.
audit_findings.explanation: The partner-share inclusion is demonstrated: $154.537m of CCJV cash less Granite's $95.9m share leaves $58.637m belonging economically to partners. Removing that amount lowers base value by about $1.04 to $59.06 per share. Even excluding all $154.537m of CCJV cash would lower base value to about $57.35 and bull value to about $64.49, leaving the no-buy conclusion unchanged. Whether Granite's own $95.9m requires only a timing discount or complete exclusion remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the bridge to parent unrestricted cash, exclude the $58.637m partner share, and determine expected distribution dates for Granite's $95.9m share so any appropriate present-value discount can be applied.

audit_findings.title: The peak anchor embeds favorable project-estimate and claim catch-ups
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.9m net parent-attributable favorable revisions, equal to 11.9% of the $158.6m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Cumulative project revisions and resolved claims enter FY2025 earnings and therefore OE; using that OE as the perpetual forecast starting point may capitalize nonrecurring prior-period benefits.
audit_findings.evidence: We also recognized more net increases from revisions in estimates due to claim settlements than in the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $44.5m of parent-attributable income from major upward revisions and $25.6m from major downward revisions, a net favorable $18.9m. It does not establish what portion of the upward revisions was nonrecurring rather than ordinary project volatility. Even removing the entire net benefit from the anchor would only lower value—approximately to $55.37 per share in the base case—so it cannot reverse the existing no-buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify the parent-attributable, after-tax portion arising specifically from settled historical claims and cumulative prior-period catch-ups, subtract only that portion from normalized OE, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $41.0m in FY2021, 37.6% of filed FY2021 D&A
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE, increasing historical OE and potentially the selected anchor or trend.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $41.0m (37.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No error is demonstrated because the residual has not been shown to qualify for add-back. The quantified amount relates to FY2021, whereas the valuation uses FY2025 latest-actual OE rather than a historical trend. It therefore has no present effect on the $158.6m anchor or reported scenario values; its possible effect is also conservative because inclusion could only increase OE.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A by asset and economic character, focusing on FY2025; rerun only if filed evidence identifies an eligible FY2025 add-back or changes the anchor-selection rule.
